_README: Hand-edited. This is the ONLY file an update to docs/lockout.html ever
requires -- scripts/build_lockout_page.py reads it and regenerates the
page; the daily workflow and a dedicated push-triggered workflow both
run that script, so editing this file and pushing to main is the whole
update. Never hand-edit docs/lockout.html itself.
FIELDS
cba_expires               -- ISO date the current agreement expires.
The agreement actually expires 11:59pm
ET that date; build_lockout_page.py adds
the time and formats every on-page date
from this field, so it's the only place
the date itself is typed -- except
docs/index.html's banner, which is
hand-maintained and can't read this file
(same reason it hand-copies the GA id);
update both if this date ever changes.
lockout_start              -- ISO date the lockout began, or null if
no lockout has started yet. Set this the
day it happens and the page switches from
a countdown to a day count automatically.
A date here that hasn't arrived yet is
treated as not-started -- the page stays
on the countdown until that day comes.
lockout_end               -- ISO date the lockout ended, or null while
it is ongoing / has not happened. Once
set, the day count freezes at the day
the stoppage reached.
regular_season_delayed_from -- ISO date the regular season was
originally scheduled to start, or null.
Set this only once games are actually
being missed -- it drives the
'service-time days at stake' figure.
updated                   -- ISO date this file was last hand-edited.
The page shows whichever is newer of this
and the newest entry below.
entries                   -- the update log. Each item needs date
(ISO), headline, summary (plain words, 1-3
sentences, no speculation presented as
fact), source_name and source_url (must be
https). Any order -- the page sorts newest
first on its own.
entries[].category          -- OPTIONAL. Drives the on-page topic
filter above this list. One of:
salary_cap, negotiations, deadlines,
players_union, owners_league, other.
Leave it off, blank, or misspell it and
the entry still renders -- it just files
under the page's "Other" filter chip.
This can never fail validation; pick the
single best-fitting value, or 'other' if
genuinely unsure.
Never invent a source, a quote, or a date. If nothing new and verified
has happened, don't add an entry.

entries.headline: Reporting: talks remain far apart over a salary cap as the Dec. 1 deadline nears
entries.summary: Yahoo Sports reported that with the current agreement expiring Dec. 1, 2026, a lockout is widely expected the next day. The owners' push for a salary cap is described as the central sticking point, with the players' union opposed and instead seeking a higher minimum salary and stronger service-time protections.

entries.headline: Reporting: owners' salary-cap proposal pairs a payroll floor with a 50-50 revenue split
entries.summary: The Boston Globe reported that owners have proposed a salary cap near $245 million together with a roughly $171 million payroll floor and a 50-50 split of revenue, which the players' union has rejected. The Globe expects owners to lock players out at midnight on Dec. 2.

entries.headline: AP: no common ground on core money issues as the Dec. 1 expiration approaches
entries.summary: The Associated Press reported that although the two sides have been bargaining since May, they still have not found agreement on the main economic issues. Owners want a salary cap and floor plus a limit on how much of a team's payroll one player can take up, while the players are pushing for wider free agency and arbitration rights, a much higher minimum salary, more revenue sharing and a penalty for teams that spend too little.

entries.headline: MLB proposes pushing the start of its salary cap and floor back to 2028
entries.summary: At a bargaining session on Tuesday, the league offered to hold off on its proposed salary cap and payroll floor until the 2028 season, saying clubs need a full offseason to adjust. Under the offer, the current luxury tax and revenue sharing rules would stay in place for 2027.

entries.headline: Players' union rejects the delayed salary-cap plan
entries.summary: In a statement, the MLBPA said delaying the cap to 2028 doesn't change its main objections, including what it called lower player pay and the loss of guaranteed contracts. The union added that players are ready to keep bargaining in good faith for a new agreement.
